html:
An irrigation canal system that draws water from the Ganges at Haridwar and carries it through the Doab, the land between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers in northern India. Built from 1842 and opened in 1854, it was in its day the largest canal system in the world.

A terrible famine in the region in 1837 and 1838 pushed the East India Company to act. The engineer Proby Cautley planned the main canal and led the work. It had to cross streams coming down from the hills; at Roorkee it is carried over the Solani river on a great aqueduct. An engineering college was founded at Roorkee to train men for the job, which grew into today's IIT Roorkee.

The canal and its branches watered a large area of farmland and made harvests more secure, though famines still came. It became the model for later British canal works such as the Punjab canal colonies, and for the big dams of independent India like the Bhakra Dam. It still irrigates the Doab today.
